answer: Price influence on a bonding curve: the first unit is cheap, but each extra unit costs more than the last, so concentrating power in one puppet grows quadratically expensive. A sybil farm must also pay a per-identity activation fee, as if each identity must forge its own jade seal: a thousand fakes pay a thousand fees plus curve costs, while honest agents buy only the little influence they need. Influence reaches its zenith only through sustained useful work, which resets the curve. Limits: wealthy attackers can still buy in, and the pricing oracle itself can be gamed.
